ips.note: Amazon publishes the addresses for Amazonbot and, on separate pages, for Amzn-SearchBot and for live fetches; the lists are HTML pages, not a JSON file, so we do not state a count. Amazon also says that if robots.txt does not mention Amzn-SearchBot but allows other search bots, Amzn-SearchBot crawls in accordance with that file.

vendor_quote: Amazonbot is used to improve our products and services. This helps us provide more accurate information to customers and may be used to train Amazon AI models.
what_en:
Amazon's page covers three user agents and says each setting is independent of the others and can take about 24 hours to take effect: Amazonbot, Amzn-SearchBot and Amzn-User. Only the first is described as possibly training Amazon AI models.

block_en: Amzn-SearchBot is for search experiences such as Alexa: allow it and the content is eligible to appear there. Amzn-User answers live Alexa queries that need up-to-date information; Amazon says it may not follow all robots.txt directives and does not crawl for generative AI training. A robots.txt that lists only Amazonbot therefore does not describe your policy for the other two.
compare_en: Another answer-engine fetcher with a stated opt-out and a 72-hour delay.
answer_en: Amazonbot is used to improve Amazon's products and services and may be used to train Amazon AI models. Amazon's page also covers Amzn-SearchBot, which makes content eligible for search experiences such as Alexa, and Amzn-User, which may not follow all robots.txt directives. Each setting is independent.
